requirements.title: TINY value follows the real model
requirements.definition: The TINY result has the value b raised to emin minus one for the real model of the same type and kind as X.

pending.TINY-positive-model-number: Initialize a real sentinel to -1.0, assign TINY(x), and assert the result is greater than 0.0 for default real and double precision controls. Mutate the intrinsic name to -TINY.
pending.TINY-MINEXPONENT-EXPONENT-relation: For default real and double precision controls, assert EXPONENT(TINY(x)) equals MINEXPONENT(x), derived from the 16.4 model value b raised to emin minus one. Mutate MINEXPONENT to MAXEXPONENT so the finite relation differs.
pending.TINY-FRACTION-RADIX-relation: For default real and double precision controls, assert FRACTION(TINY(x)) equals REAL(1,KIND(x))/REAL(RADIX(x),KIND(x)): from b raised to emin minus one, FRACTION is b inverse and EXPONENT is emin. The RADIX integer b is converted to the same real kind as x, whose radix is b and whose model exactly represents 1 and b for this model-parameter relation. Mutate RADIX to RADIX plus one so the exact relation differs.
pending.TINY-exact-numeric-model-value-latitude: No portable exact numeric oracle: p5 names b and emin from the processor real model, so their concrete values differ across conforming processors. Future fixtures use model relations such as EXPONENT(TINY(x)) equals MINEXPONENT(x), not hard-coded decimal constants.
